what_its_for: Prochlorperazine is used to treat severe nausea and vomiting. It is also used to treat symptoms of certain mental health conditions such as schizophrenia, including anxiety, agitation, and disordered thinking. Your doctor may also prescribe it for other reasons.
how_to_take: Take this medicine exactly as your doctor tells you. It comes in different forms: tablets you swallow, suppositories you insert into your rectum, and injections given in a clinic or hospital. Swallow tablets whole with a full glass of water. You may take tablets with or without food, but taking them with food may help prevent stomach upset. For suppositories, unwrap and gently insert the pointed end into your rectum. Wash your hands before and after. Do not crush, chew, or break the tablets.
dosing: The dose your doctor prescribes will depend on why you are taking this medicine and your overall health. For nausea and vomiting in adults, the usual tablet dose is 5 to 10 mg taken 3 to 4 times a day. For anxiety, the usual dose is 5 mg taken 2 to 3 times a day. For more serious mental health conditions, doses may be higher. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store tablets and suppositories at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep them away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store them in the bathroom. Store suppositories in the refrigerator if they become too soft. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of any unused or expired medicine safely — ask your pharmacist about local drug take-back programs.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medicine, as it can increase drowsiness and dizziness and may cause dangerous side effects. Avoid driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing anything that requires you to be fully alert until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid getting overheated or becoming dehydrated, especially in hot weather or during exercise, as this medicine can affect your body's ability to regulate temperature. Avoid taking antacids or anti-diarrhea medicines within 2 hours of taking prochlorperazine, as they can reduce how well it works. Tell all your doctors and dentists that you take this medicine before any procedures.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: uncontrollable movements of your face, tongue, eyes, arms, or legs (these can be signs of a serious condition called tardive dyskinesia or an acute dystonic reaction); muscle stiffness, high fever, confusion, or fast heartbeat (signs of a rare but dangerous condition called Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome); fainting or irregular heartbeat; difficulty swallowing or breathing; severe skin rash or yellowing of the skin or eyes; unusual bruising or bleeding; signs of infection such as fever, chills, or sore throat; or if you feel much more confused or restless than usual. Also call your doctor if your nausea or vomiting does not improve after a few days.
when_it_works: For nausea and vomiting, this medicine usually starts working within 30 to 60 minutes after you take a tablet or use a suppository. For anxiety or mental health symptoms, it may take several days to a few weeks before you notice the full benefit. Keep taking your medicine even if you feel better unless your doctor tells you to stop.
special_populations: Older adults: Use with caution. Older people are more sensitive to side effects such as dizziness, falls, confusion, and movement problems. This medicine is generally not recommended as a first choice in elderly patients. Children: This medicine can be used in children over 2 years of age or weighing more than 20 pounds (9 kg) for nausea and vomiting, but only at doses prescribed by a doctor. It should not be used in children under 2 years old. Pregnancy: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Using it near the time of delivery may cause temporary movement problems or withdrawal symptoms in the newborn. Breastfeeding: This medicine may pass into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding while taking this medicine. Kidney or liver disease: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver problems, as your dose may need to be adjusted.
